channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Transferência de votos de Bolsonaro para Flávio nas pesquisas é ‘muito rápida’, diz diretora do Datafolha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads Lula in a Datafolha poll (46% to 45%) in a hypothetical second-round scenario for the first time, but institute director Luciana Chong cautions that the lead is not yet indicative of a trend, citing high rejection rates for both candidates and low voter engagement. Anti-Petismo and negative economic perception, driven by cost-of-living pressures, are hurting Lula, while candidates like Caiado and Zema also benefit from anti-PT sentiment. Polarization and government weariness create an open and uncertain outlook for 2026.

item.title: Com Lula no Planalto, INSS chega ao quarto presidente em menos de quatro anos
item.description: The INSS had four presidents under Lula's government, all marked by corruption scandals or management failures. Glauco Wamburg was dismissed in 2023 for misuse of air tickets; Alessandro Stefanutto was removed in April 2025 after a billion-dollar fraud scheme; Gilberto Waller was fired after eleven months for opposing the Previdência minister and worsening the backlog, which reached 3.1 million. Ana Cristina Silveira, a career servant, was appointed to resolve the crisis, as PF and MPF investigations continue.

item.title: Ala do PT quer explorar acordo da CPMI do Master para atrasar análise de veto ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: A PT faction aims to exploit an alleged Senate President Davi Alcolumbre deal to bury the Master CPMI in order to delay the analysis of Lula’s veto on the Dosimetry Bill. The group plans to provoke debates on the issue to hinder the veto’s appraisal, as the governing coalition believes Alcolumbre agreed to schedule the veto only if the opposition did not push for the CPMI. PT lawmakers acknowledge that not all allies may support the tactic, as some favor burying the CPMI even before its formation.

item.title: ‘Desunião Brasil’: lançamento de Pablo Marçal ao Senado potencializa racha da direita em SP
item.description: The potential Senate candidacy of Pablo Marçal in São Paulo, despite his ineligibility, is deepening divisions within the state's right-wing, with União Brasil betting on a reversal of his disqualification by the TSE. His entry threatens existing agreements and could sideline federal deputy Guilherme Derrite (PP-SP), creating friction within the União Progressista federation. Although viewed as a strong digital mobilizer with 13 million followers, Marçal faces resistance due to legal hurdles and perceptions of undermining established alliances.

item.title: Zema diz detestar políticos e que o diabo mandou o PT a Minas
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), pre-candidate for Presidency, stated he detests politicians and that the devil sent the PT to Minas Gerais, referring to former governor Fernando Pimentel. He criticized the PT administration for salary delays, non-payment of 13th salary, failure to transfer ICMS and IPVA funds to municipalities, and for blacklisting 240,000 public servants by deducting loan payments without paying banks. Zema said his entry into politics was ironic, driven by the 2015-2016 economic crisis, and defended his Minas Gerais administration as scandal- and corruption-free, with no relatives appointed to public office.

item.title: Pupilo de Valdemar Costa Neto intensifica articulação para disputar vaga ao Senado por SP
item.description: André do Prado, president of the São Paulo State Legislature (Alesp) and ally of Valdemar Costa Neto, is intensifying his efforts to secure a Senate seat in São Paulo after being passed over for the vice-presidential spot on Tarcísio de Freitas’ re-election ticket. While the governor expressed support for Prado’s candidacy for the second Senate seat, he stated the final decision rests with Eduardo Bolsonaro, who is currently abroad. Prado’s backing of the PL and his role in ensuring governability for Tarcísio — including the privatization of Sabesp — has strengthened his position as the bolsonarist faction’s preferred candidate.

item.title: Presidente do INSS, Gilberto Waller, é demitido após 11 meses
item.description: The president of the INSS (National Institute of Social Security), Gilberto Waller, was dismissed after 11 months in office and replaced by career civil servant Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, who previously served as deputy executive secretary of the Ministry of Social Security. The change aims to accelerate benefit analysis and streamline internal processes, aligned with President Lula’s goal of clearing the backlog. Waller had succeeded Alessandro Stefanutto, who was under investigation in Operation Sem Desconto over alleged fraud in pensions and retirement benefits.

item.title: Zema fala em “crise moral” e critica Judiciário: “Contaminado”
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for president, stated that Brazil is experiencing 'the greatest moral crisis in history' and criticized the Judiciary, claiming the 'last resort' of the population 'has been contaminated'. He also denounced a 'party of the untouchables' in Brasília, accused the Supreme Court of 'smelling bad' for years and now revealing corruption, and said there are 'criminals' in government, fueling public outrage beyond 2018 levels.

item.title: Messias quebra resistências e chega a 48 votos por vaga no STF após 'cinco meses na chuva'
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias now has 48 secured votes to become an STF minister, surpassing the 41 needed for approval. His support has grown due to backing from evangelical senators, Bolsonaro-appointed ministers André Mendonça and Kássio Nunes Marques, and STF dean Gilmar Mendes, despite initial opposition from Flávio Dino and attempts by Davi Alcolumbre to delay the vote.

item.title: Rio, laboratório do colapso
item.description: Rio de Janeiro is portrayed as a laboratory of Brazil's political, social, and institutional collapse, where crises in security, health, education, and corruption intensify and intertwine. Political scientist Josué Medeiros, from UFRJ and UFRRJ, coordinates observatories analyzing these phenomena, highlighting the fragility of democracy and the erosion of public services in the state. The text suggests that what happens in Rio anticipates national trends for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Agora é lei: vacina contra o câncer passa a ter prioridade no Sistema Único de Saúde
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.385/2026, which prioritizes cancer vaccines, oncological drugs, and advanced therapy technologies in the Unified Health System (SUS), ensuring free and accelerated access. The law promotes national innovation through support for domestic production, AI, public-private partnerships, and reduced import dependence, aligning with international best practices.

item.title: Quem é Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, nova presidente do INSS
item.description: Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, a career INSS servant since 2003 and former president of the CRPS, has been appointed as the new president of the National Institute of Social Security (INSS), replacing Gilberto Waller, who was dismissed following a fraud scheme that diverted up to R$ 6.3 billion from retirees. Her leadership is noted for expertise in social security resource analysis and a 21% increase in service backlogs from May 2025 to February 2026 — a factor that influenced the Lula government’s decision. The appointment comes amid efforts to restore credibility to the INSS after corruption scandals in the social security system.

item.title: Governo troca comando da presidência do INSS
item.description: The Minister of Social Security, Wolney Queiroz Maciel, announced the appointment of Ana Cristina Viana Silveira as the new president of INSS, replacing Gilberto Waller. A career servant since 2003 and former deputy executive secretary of the ministry, she previously led the CRPS from 2023 to 2026, doubling its capacity to analyze appeals. The appointment strengthens female representation in INSS leadership and aims to speed up benefit processing and streamline internal procedures.

item.title: Lula investe em imagem de 'rato de academia' para driblar críticas à idade, diz jornal britânico
item.description: The British newspaper The Guardian published a report analyzing President Lula's (PT) communication strategy, which involves frequently sharing images of himself exercising to counter criticism about his advanced age of 80. The report suggests this exposure aims to convey to voters that the petista maintains physical vigor and health, attempting to alleviate concerns about his capacity to govern due to age.

item.title: ‘Se querem meu número, peçam ao Valdemar’, diz Renato Bolsonaro sobre ciumeira no PL
item.description: Renato Bolsonaro, younger brother of former President Jair Bolsonaro and PL pre-candidate for federal deputy, states that the use of ballot number '2222' was authorized by Valdemar Costa Neto and Jair Bolsonaro, and that internal criticism stems from vanity. He says he is focused on the federal deputy race but is available for a Senate run if the party and his brother decide so.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: A vantagem de Lula evaporou
item.description: The Datafolha poll featured on Meio-Dia em Brasília shows a technical tie between President Lula (PT) and candidates Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Romeu Zema (Novo), and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) in potential 2026 presidential runoff scenarios. The program also covered the latest meeting of the Congressional Parliamentary Inquiry Commission (CPI). Lula’s previous polling advantage appears to have evaporated, signaling a highly polarized electoral landscape.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro ‘atrapalha’ e direita deve focar em Lula, diz Ciro Nogueira
item.description: Ciro Nogueira, president of the PP, stated that Eduardo Bolsonaro 'hinders' the right by creating internal disputes, especially by criticizing Nikolas Ferreira, and urged focus on opposing President Lula's government. He emphasized that the right should prioritize security, health, education, and competitiveness, reducing polarization and pointless debates. The remarks came as the PP discusses its 2026 positioning and maintains dialogue with Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: O nome de Lula para tentar tirar o governo do Rio das mãos da direita
item.description: Former Rio State Assembly president André Ceciliano announces his candidacy for the Fluminense government via an indirect election in the Alerj, with backing from the Lula administration. He aims to exploit divisions among Bolsonarists to challenge Douglas Ruas (PL) ahead of a direct election against Eduardo Paes (PSD). The STF has already voted 4-1 in favor of the indirect election, awaiting a final ruling.

item.title: Filas em ano eleitoral levaram governo Lula a trocar comando do INSS
item.description: The Lula government replaced the leadership of the INSS due to growing benefit queues that damage the administration's image and could be exploited by political opponents in the 2026 elections. Gilberto Waller, former INSS president, was dismissed for failing to resolve the backlog, despite having stabilized management after the pension fraud scandal. Ana Cristina Silveira, former deputy executive secretary of the Ministry of Social Security, assumes the role with the mandate to streamline services and reduce queues, which rose 21% in nine months according to Camila Bomfim's blog.

item.title: Quase 130 milhões de pessoas têm débitos bancários, e BC vê superendividamento como 'problema crescente' no Brasil
item.description: Nearly 130 million Braziliors have bank debts, representing 74% of the population with a banking relationship, according to the Central Bank, which warns of growing overindebtedness. The rise is tied to the expansion of unsecured credit, such as personal loans (which more than tripled since 2020) and credit card revolving debt, reaching 53 million people in 2024. The Lula government is evaluating measures to reduce indebtedness, including debt renegotiation with interest discounts of up to 90% and potential use of FGTS funds for debt repayment.

item.title: Flávio critica Lula com imagens gravadas durante gestão de Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro used footage from 2021, during his father Jair Bolsonaro's administration, to criticize Lula's government, claiming a 'serious crisis' of indebtedness and hunger in Brazil. The post drew reactions from ministers like Guilherme Boulos and Gleisi Hoffmann, who highlighted the contradiction of using Bolsonaro-era images to attack the current government. A Datafolha poll shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, with the senator slightly ahead in a hypothetical runoff.

item.title: Três legendas exibem propaganda partidária nesta semana
item.description: This week, the parties Republicans, Brazil Union, and Sustainability Network are airing free partisan propaganda on TV and radio on March 14, 16, and 18, 2026, according to the electoral calendar. Republicans have 11 minutes distributed across the week, Sustainability Network has 3.5 minutes on Saturday, and Brazil Union has only 0.5 minute on Thursday. The distribution complies with TSE Ordinance No. 460/2025, which allows up to 20 minutes for Brazil Union and Republicans and 5 minutes for the Network in the first half of 2026.

item.title: Lula demite presidente do INSS
item.description: The president of INSS, Gilberto Waller, was dismissed after eleven months in office and replaced by Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, a career civil servant since 2003 and former president of the CRPS. The change aims to speed up benefit analysis and simplify internal processes, with the Minister of Social Security praising her technical profile and commitment to leaving no Brazilian behind.

item.title: Direita se mobiliza para barrar nome do PT no TCU
item.description: Right-wing sectors in the Chamber are mobilizing to block the PT-backed candidate for a seat at the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU), despite the support of House Speaker Hugo Motta. The effort includes building a broad front against the petista candidate, with reports that one applicant has directly persuaded rivals to withdraw to consolidate opposition. The already politicized election has become increasingly tense and potentially explosive in Brasília’s behind-the-scenes negotiations.

item.title: Comissão da Câmara sabatina indicados ao TCU nesta 2ª feira
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Finance and Taxation Committee holds a hearing this Monday (April 13, 2026) with seven candidates vying for a seat at the TCU following the retirement of Minister Aroldo Cedraz. Government-backed candidate Odair Cunha (PT-MG) enjoys the support of Chamber President Hugo Motta and a broad coalition of parties. After the hearing, approved candidates will be voted on in secret on Tuesday (April 14) and sent to the Senate for confirmation or rejection.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Lula vai à Europa em meio a pesquisas eleitorais e cenário econômico negativos
item.description: Lula travels to Europe amid unfavorable electoral polls and ahead of the release of three new national surveys. Meanwhile, the government prepares the 2027 Budget Guidelines Law with a primary surplus target of 0.5% of GDP, facing analyst skepticism about achieving it without accounting maneuvers. The trip aims to secure economic and political support, particularly regarding the Mercosul-EU agreement, while Brazil’s record tax burden in 2025 strengthens opposition criticism.

item.title: Centrão resiste a Zema como vice de Flávio
item.description: Centrão leaders are resisting support for Romeu Zema as Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate in the 2026 presidential race, preferring Senator Tereza Cristina (PP-MS) for the position. The bloc fears that aligning with Zema could weaken their influence and fail to deliver expected political benefits. The resistance reflects ongoing negotiations within the government base to define the major ticket.

item.title: Queda de Orbán divide direita e anima esquerda no Brasil
item.description: The defeat of Viktor Orbán in Hungary’s elections after 16 years in power sparked reactions in Brazil, dividing the right and energizing the left. The opposition’s landslide victory, with over 77% voter turnout and a supermajority enabling constitutional changes, was seen by Brazilian progressives as a rejection of authoritarianism and religious conservatism. Meanwhile, Brazil’s right, which had viewed Orbán as an ideological ally, expressed concern over the weakening of international partners in their traditional values agenda.

item.title: Vice-presidente do PT convida Silvio Almeida, indiciado por assédio, para cargo no RJ
item.description: The national vice-president of the PT, Washington Quaquá, invited former minister Silvio Almeida — indicted for sexual harassment in November 2025 and denounced by the PGR in March 2026 — to coordinate the Museum of Black Slavery in the Atlantic and participate in UniMar in Maricá. Almeida was removed from the federal government in late 2024 following allegations, including one by former Minister Anielle Franco, who is now running for Chamber of Deputies in 2026. Quaquá had previously defended Almeida, citing 'Christian forgiveness' and criticizing the 'politics of outrage and cancellation'.

item.title: Lula paga o preço por casos de corrupção no país, diz presidente do PT sobre queda de popularidade
item.description: PT president Edinho Silva attributed the recent decline in President Lula's popularity to an 'avalanche of corruption allegations' in Brazil, citing the Banco Master case and the INSS CPMI investigation. He argued that the public tends to associate these scandals with the government, even without direct involvement, and that Lula is 'paying the price' for a hostile political climate. Despite this, Edinho defended Lula's re-election bid in 2026.

item.title: Hungria, Colômbia e Peru: Planalto monitora influência de Trump sobre eleições
item.description: The Lula government is monitoring elections in Hungary, Colombia, and Peru as gauges of global right-wing influence and external actor interference—particularly from Donald Trump—on Brazil’s 2026 presidential race. Viktor Orbán’s defeat in Hungary is seen as a potential weakening of international Trumpism, despite explicit U.S. support. In Peru, a fragmented first round leading to a runoff between Keiko Fujimori and Rafael López Aliaga keeps the Planalto on high alert due to the competitiveness of right-wing candidates and risks of external meddling.

item.title: Flávio apresenta seu candidato no Rio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro introduced state deputy Douglas Ruas as the PL's candidate for Guanabara Palace in Rio de Janeiro. He stated that the party understands the people's desire to defeat crime with courage. The event underscores the right's strategy to expand its electoral base in the state.

item.title: Ministros do STF articulam votos para Messias no Senado
item.description: STF ministers are lobbying for sufficient votes to approve Jorge Messias’s nomination to the Supreme Court, assessing that support is adequate for Senate advancement. The confirmation hearing before the Senate’s Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) is scheduled for April 29, with Senator Weverton Rocha as rapporteur. While allies of Senate President Davi Alcolumbre deny direct involvement, the government’s coordination and backing from ministers including Kassio Nunes Marques, André Mendonça, Gilmar Mendes, and Cristiano Zanin suggest a clear path to approval.

item.title: Datafolha: clima não é de desespero, mas sinal de alerta acendeu no Palácio do Planalto
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows Lula's approval dropped to 45% and disapproval rose to 51%, with him technically tied against Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema in both first and second rounds. Allies warn the government is watching opponents campaign without effective public contact, noting Lula's social media structure remains unimplemented while Bolsonaro's is already advanced.

item.title: Indicados a vaga de ministro do TCU passam por sabatina na Câmara nesta segunda
item.description: Seven candidates for a ministerial vacancy at the TCU are undergoing a hearing in the Chamber of Deputies' Finance and Taxation Committee on Monday (13). Odair Cunha (PT-MG) is seen as the frontrunner behind the scenes, backed by multiple parties and aligned with Chamber President Hugo Motta. The vacancy, opened after the retirement of Minister Aroldo Cedraz, will proceed to a plenary vote following the hearing.

item.title: Petistas comemoram derrota na Hungria de Viktor Orbán, líder da extrema direita global: 'Aliado de Bolsonaro'
item.description: Brazilian Workers' Party politicians celebrated Viktor Orbán's defeat in the Hungarian elections, labeling him a key early ally of Jair Bolsonaro and a symbol of global far-right advancement. José Guimarães, head of Lula's political articulation, stated the result signifies a democratic victory and a precursor to Brazil reaffirming democratic values in the 2026 elections. Orbán's loss is seen as a sign of declining obscurantism and right-wing extremism fueled by social media disinformation.

item.title: Jornal espanhol coloca Pedro como opção de ‘camisa 9’ para Ancelotti na Copa do Mundo
item.description: Forward Pedro shone in the derby against Fluminense, scoring two goals and gaining attention from European media. Spanish outlet As named him a potential option for Brazil's number 9 shirt in the 2026 World Cup under Carlo Ancelotti, citing his versatility and goal-scoring form. Pedro aims to secure a national team call-up following strong performances for Flamengo under Leonardo Jardim.

item.title: Eleições na Hungria: líderes repercutem derrota de Orbán
item.description: International leaders congratulated Peter Magyar on his victory in Hungary's legislative elections, highlighting the result as a sign of electorate adherence to European values after 16 years of Viktor Orbán's government. The win was seen as a significant democratic movement in Europe, emphasizing high voter turnout and Hungary's repositioning within the European Union. In Brazil, PT politicians celebrated the outcome.

item.title: Centrão rejeita Zema como vice de Flávio e vê fala sobre Nordeste como "bomba eleitoral"
item.description: Centrão leaders reject Romeu Zema as a potential running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro, calling his remarks about the Northeast a 'disaster' and an 'electoral bomb' that opponents, especially Lula's government, could exploit. Despite the bloc's preference for Tereza Cristina, Zema remains the favored choice of Flávio Bolsonaro's hard core, with the two sharing an ironic joint video on social media after a technical tie in a Datafolha poll.

item.title: Julgamento de Denarium volta ao TSE sob tentativa de adiamento
item.description: The TSE resumes on Tuesday (April 14, 2026) the trial that could invalidate the ticket of Antonio Denarium (Republicanos) and Edilson Damião (União-Brasil) in Roraima, after two prior postponements. Allies are seeking another adjournment via a new request for vista, with Minister Antonio Carlos Ferreira cited as a possible instigator, coinciding with the election of Nunes Marques as the new TSE president on the same day. On Friday (April 10, 2026), Damião was approached by the Federal Police upon arriving in Brasília on a private jet contracted by the Roraima government, though the state stated the procedure was routine and without irregularities.

item.title: Agenda da semana: Lula sanciona PNE e Durigan viaja aos EUA
item.description: This week, President Lula signs the childcare reimbursement for outsourced federal workers and the National Education Plan (PNE), while Finance Minister Fernando Haddad (or another unnamed official) travels to the U.S. for meetings with the IMF, Chinese financial leaders, and the G7. Meanwhile, the judiciary moves forward with interrogating former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro and the STF prepares to rule on compulsory retirement at age 75, highlighting ongoing tensions between the executive, legislative, and judicial branches.

item.title: Neta de Lula ironiza Flávio Bolsonaro com dança da rachadinha
item.description: Lula's granddaughter, Bia Lula, posted an AI-generated Instagram video mocking Flávio Bolsonaro with the 'rachadinha dance,' referencing the salary kickback scheme investigated when he was a state deputy in RJ. The video responds to Flávio's use of dance in pre-campaign events, a tactic the PT is using to undermine his image. Flávio is in a technical tie with Lula in 2026 polls, with 45.8% versus 45.5% in a potential runoff.

item.title: Fim do mistério: quem deu a paca para Lula e Janja
item.description: O Globo reported that businessman Emílio Odebrecht, a longtime friend of Lula, was responsible for giving paca meat to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and his wife Janja. Odebrecht claims to be Brazil’s largest paca breeder and regularly gifts the meat to the presidential couple. The report resolves the mystery surrounding the origin of the meat served at a recent event.

item.title: TSE retoma julgamento de ex-governador de Roraima depois de cinco meses
item.description: The TSE will resume on Tuesday the trial of an action against former Roraima governor Antonio Denarium and current governor Edilson Damião, which had been suspended since November 2023 after Minister Nunes Marques requested a view. During the interval, Denarium left office to run for election and Damião, then vice-governor, assumed the position. Two votes have already been cast in favor of cassation for both; if a majority upholds this, Damião would lose office and Denarium would become ineligible. Both were removed by the Roraima TRE for improper use of public machinery during the electoral period and appealed to the TSE.

item.title: 83,8% dos eleitores do Paraná aprovam o governo Ratinho Junior
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on April 13, 2026 shows that 83.8% of Paraná voters approve of Governor Ratinho Junior’s (PSD) administration, with 34% rating it as excellent and 38.3% as good. The poll interviewed 1,500 people across 56 municipalities from April 10–12, 2026, with a margin of error of ±2.6 percentage points and 95% confidence level, registered with the TSE under PR-06559/2026 and funded by the Liberal Party (PL).

item.title: Moro lidera com folga a disputa ao governo do PR, diz pesquisa
item.description: Sergio Moro leads the race for governor of Paraná with between 46% and 52.5% of voting intentions, according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey released on April 13, 2026. The poll, conducted between April 10 and 12 with 1,500 voters across 56 municipalities, has a margin of error of 2.6 percentage points and a 95% confidence level. The study was funded by the PL and registered with the TSE under number PR-06559/2026.

item.title: STF tem ar de guerra aberta, irritação de Carmem e divergências explícitas
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Federal Court is experiencing heightened tension, with explicit divisions among ministers and visible irritation from Minister Carmen Lúcia during the ruling on the format of the new Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election. Court President Edson Fachin strives to maintain balance amid a tacit conflict between factions of the Court.

item.title: PSD nasce de ruptura com o DEM e vira força regional em 13 anos
item.description: The Social Democratic Party (PSD) was founded on April 13, 2011, by Gilberto Kassab after his departure from the DEM, aiming to occupy a centrist space in Brazil's polarized politics. Initially comprising 55 federal deputies, 2 senators, and 2 governors, the party attracted figures from multiple parties and consolidated as a regional force, celebrating its 13th anniversary in 2026 with a trajectory marked by pragmatism and alliances with governments of diverse ideologies.

item.title: Juro alto é o preço de um desequilíbrio fiscal desde 2014, diz Bentes
item.description: Fabio Bentes, chief economist at CNC, argues that record household indebtedness in Brazil stems from a fiscal imbalance since 2014, worsened by years of monetary tightening. He states that elevated interest rates are the price of this imbalance, with household debt reaching 80.4% in March — the highest in the historical series — and delinquency at 29.6%, up 1.0 percentage point year-on-year. The Lula government plans to release up to R$ 7 billion from FGTS and is studying a new Desenrola Brasil program to ease household debt.

item.title: Relatório de trabalho por apps reduz regras; governo cobra proteção
item.description: The PLP 152/2025 opinion reduces regulations for app-based work, maintaining autonomous status and setting a R$ 8.50 per ride floor, sparking conflict with the Lula government, which demands higher pay and stronger social protections, including night/weekend premiums and broader accident coverage. The text caps platform fees at 30% and lowers social security contributions, criticized by the Executive for weakening collective bargaining and worker safeguards.
